correctness.rationale: The exact square of an arbitrary radical element is computed in the PBW basis; the resulting equations isolate five exhaustive and disjoint characteristic/parameter conditions. Each irreducible component or split quadric is explicitly described, with Grothendieck classes computed via disjoint affine strata. The three consecutive graded linear-form multiplication maps have ranks 1, 2, 1, forcing rank 4 by the square-zero upper bound, and lower-degree cases yield ranks 2, 1, 0. Full PBW arithmetic enumeration and matrix Gaussian elimination verified all counts and rank strata over all nonzero parameters in fields of sizes 2,3,4,5 (ten exhaustive cases). Only reduced geometries are claimed; finite checks are not used as proofs for arbitrary fields.

originality.rationale: The assessed contribution is the complete mixed-degree square-zero variety of the 8-dimensional three-generator equal-parameter quantum exterior algebra, with five deformation/characteristic regimes, reduced components, motivic classes and exact regular multiplication rank polynomials. Bergh–Erdmann (2008) develops rank varieties, and Bergh–Erdmann–Jorgensen (2019) studies Jordan types for modules and linear forms. Those results already explain regular-module freeness along certain linear forms, which is not claimed here, but do not provide the mixed-degree square-zero cone or its counts. Published-record and literature searches found no exact or stronger coverage. Priority remains subject to unlocated historical literature. A previously compared square-zero classification of the 12-dimensional two-generator (3,4)-truncation has the same broad invariant but concerns a nonisomorphic algebra with different PBW equations and no implication of this three-generator (2,2,2)-exterior classification.
residual_risks: The historical literature on nilpotent varieties of small quantum complete intersections is not exhaustively indexed; an equivalent statement or a stronger theorem may have escaped searches.

The regular-linear-part acyclicity follows from known freeness/projectivity principles in the classical parameter regimes and is not independently original; originality relies on the mixed-degree full-locus and arithmetic geometry statements.
Potential implicit coverage by general algorithms for equations of square-zero elements in finite-dimensional PBW algebras remains possible, although no decisive specific source was identified.

value.rationale: The eight-dimensional three-generator quantum exterior algebra is the first natural constant-parameter PBW truncation where degree-one/degree-two interaction is nontrivial. The theorem gives a complete five-regime moduli-geometric classification over arbitrary fields, a sharp primitive-fourth-root resonance separate from the exterior case, Grothendieck classes and all finite-field regular-differential ranks. These determine natural nilpotent and homological invariants and are not selected arbitrary isolated numerical cases. The classical linear-form freeness input is explicitly separated from the newly assessed mixed-degree zero-square geometry.
